checks: The simplex determinant is q!, so its q-volume is one. Every one-cap strict residual in 2T with upper cutoff s∈(0,2) is a full-dimensional similarity cut of volume s^q. On all real heights the smaller upper cutoff is at most one, so the three closed caps cover the entire real product.

Only the integer bases −1,0,1 occur. For the three given caps their residual roots are 1+az, 1−az and (2^q−1)^{1/q}; the last exceeds one for q≥2. This gives the exact three root obstacles, all positive.
The nonnegative convex heights satisfy h_0≥1 and h_−+h_+≥2h_0. Jensen and strict convexity give cost at least 3 with equality only at the feasible constant threshold one.

The supporting-row inequalities and multipliers are explicit. At zero slopes, the two size-q transfers have signed base moment zero. Height stationarity is q−3q+2q=0 at the source and q−q=0 at each destination. Complementarity holds, and the retained center mass q supplies the third column of the row, so all three probabilities are 1/3.

The selected cap H_+ is one of the minimizing residual caps at the source, with roots 1−a,1,1+a and exact mean one. Strict convexity gives the positive volume defect Δ_q(a)/3 and all three mixed cap masses as stated. Exact arithmetic independently checked these identities for q=2–10 at a=1/2. The equal original fibers have exact Minkowski comparison, and no critical or below-target cap premise is used.
